rv.q: The two plays are worlds apart: The politics, richly populated ensemble and pinpoint sociology of the early work gave way to a more sentimental vehicle for three stars in the popular backstage melodrama.
And for whatever reason, everyone in “The Country Girl” seems to be operating on his or her own isolating frequency.
The credible production lacks the histrionics necessary to fire the melodrama.

cn.t: Mike Nichols' revival of Odets' backstage drama receives a mixed reception, with critics divided on whether the star-studded production breathes life into the 1950 play or leaves it feeling inert.
